title: flashcard
description: A review session of flashcards: the question, revealed on tap on the device, then how well you knew it; the ratings go to the agent in one message at the end, and it schedules the next review.

front.description: The question side: “How do you say “receipt”?”, “What does this sign mean?”. Large text; long fronts drop to body size.

example.description: A line under the answer: an example sentence with its translation, a mnemonic: “¿Me da el recibo?” Can I have the receipt?

hint.description: A nudge shown under the question after Show Hint (local): “Starts with r, six letters”.

media.description: An image or audio clip on the front: a road sign, a bone, a word to hear. `alt` is read before the question.

front_lang.description: BCP 47 language of the front, so VoiceOver uses the right voice.

intervals.description: When the card comes back after each rating, from the agent’s scheduler: “1 min”, “10 min”, “1 day”, “4 days”. Shown under each rating. Omit to show the ratings alone.

cards.description: The cards of this session (or of this batch of a longer one), in order. All of them are in the payload, so rating needs no round trip. Empty when nothing is due (the empty state).

done.description: Cards rated in earlier batches of this session: 0 for a session that fits in one payload.

total.description: Cards in the whole session: the “20” in “3 of 20”.

due_today.description: Cards due today in the whole deck, for the subtitle.

progress.description: Where the session is. The client shows done + the current card’s position, of total.

next_due.description: When the next cards are due. Required when `cards` is empty. The empty state and the end of the session say it: “Next cards are due tomorrow.”
